1| package ingest
2| 
3| import (
4| 	"crypto/sha256"
5| 	"encoding/binary"
6| 	"encoding/hex"
7| )
8| 
9| // batchKey fingerprints one accepted batch for duplicate detection.
10| // The key covers tenant, producer, and the content digest, but
11| // deliberately NOT the receive timestamp: a producer that retries the
12| // same batch after a network error must collide with its earlier
13| // self, and timestamps would make every retry unique.
14| func batchKey(tenant, producer string, payload []byte) string {
15| 	h := sha256.New()
16| 	h.Write([]byte(tenant))
17| 	h.Write([]byte{0})
18| 	h.Write([]byte(producer))
19| 	h.Write([]byte{0})
20| 	var n [8]byte
21| 	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(n[:], uint64(len(payload)))
22| 	h.Write(n[:])
23| 	h.Write(payload)
24| 	return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil)[:16])
25| }
26| 
27| // shardFor buckets a key into one of the dedupe shards. Sharding is
28| // stable across restarts so a key seen before a crash lands in the
29| // same shard's window after recovery, and a fleet of edges spreads
30| // keys identically for the same shard count.
31| func shardFor(key string, shards int) int {
32| 	var v uint32
33| 	for i := 0; i < 4 && i < len(key); i++ {
34| 		v = v<<8 | uint32(key[i])
35| 	}
36| 	return int(v % uint32(shards))
37| }

8| // dedupeWindow is the shipped default for how long a batch key is

11| // the fleet posture, not a per-edge promise.
12| const dedupeWindow = 120 * time.Second

14| // window holds recently seen keys with their first-seen times. One
15| // window per shard keeps lock contention bounded under burst load.
16| type window struct {
17| 	mu   sync.Mutex
18| 	seen map[string]time.Time
19| }
20| 
21| // duplicate reports whether the key was already seen inside the
22| // window, recording it either way. Expiry is lazy: stale entries are
23| // dropped by the scan that finds them rather than by a sweeper, so an
24| // idle shard costs nothing until traffic returns to it.
25| func (w *window) duplicate(key string, now time.Time, ttl time.Duration) bool {
26| 	w.mu.Lock()
27| 	defer w.mu.Unlock()
28| 	if first, ok := w.seen[key]; ok && now.Sub(first) <= ttl {
29| 		return true
30| 	}
31| 	for k, t := range w.seen {
32| 		if now.Sub(t) > ttl {
33| 			delete(w.seen, k)
34| 		}
35| 	}
36| 	w.seen[key] = now
37| 	return false
38| }
